result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.dag_to_branching()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Unfold a directed acyclic graph into a branching (forest) of its root-to-leaf paths. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.dag_to_branching()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Unfold a directed acyclic graph into a branching (forest) of its root-to-leaf paths. title: >- [Graph.dag_to_branching()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Unfold a directed acyclic graph into a branching (forest) of its root-to-leaf paths. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Unfold a directed acyclic graph into a branching (forest) of its root-to-leaf paths. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L58638-L58717){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.dag_to_branching() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![DAG to branching](/assets/graphs/dag-to-branching.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a diamond DAG in which A points to B and C, and both point to D (accent color). Right: dag_to_branching() unrolls every root-to-leaf path into a tree: A leads to A/B and A/C, and D, reached along both paths, appears twice, as A/B/D and A/C/D in the accent color. Each new node is labeled with its path, and the result is a branching." width="100%"} Every path from a root (a node without incoming edges) to a leaf (a node without outgoing edges) becomes a path of the result, and paths that share a prefix share their nodes, so the result is a forest: the DAG "unrolled" so that no node has two parents. Nodes reachable along several paths are duplicated, once per distinct path prefix. This turns a DAG into a tree for algorithms and visualizations that need one (a family tree with shared ancestors drawn as a tree, a decision process, or a call graph expanded into a call tree). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new directed forest. Each node is labeled with its path from the root, such as `"A/B/D"`, and stores the ID of the original node in the attribute `"source"`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected or has a cycle. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The root-to-leaf paths are inserted into a prefix tree (trie), as in NetworkX's `dag_to_branching`. The result can be exponentially larger than the DAG, since the number of paths can grow exponentially. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a diamond, D is reached through B and through C, so it appears twice: ::: {#b82b1846 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D")]) tree = g.dag_to_branching() sorted(tree.get_label_from_id(n) for n in tree.get_node_ids()), tree.is_branching() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['A', 'A/B', 'A/B/D', 'A/C', 'A/C/D'], True) ``` ::: :::
